title: Modernize pager onramp and burn decomposition playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Objective: Reduce actionable pager noise from SLO burn-rate alerts while preserving fast detection of real capacity regressions.

Background: Recent capacity incidents (Jan–Feb 2026) showed repeated high-frequency burn-rate flapping causing noisy pages for on-call engineers. Existing mitigations (shorter burn windows, static suppression) either delay detection or fail to generalize across multi-tenant workloads. This ticket consolidates postmortem action items into an implementable playbook: a set of safe, testable changes and a staged rollout plan.

Scope: Pager onramp (how a metric escalates from metric -> alert -> page), burn-rate decomposition (separating global vs. customer-local impact), short-term cooling policies after autoscaler oscillation, and observability changes (dashboards and annotation). Does not cover long-term ML-based alert classifier (separate ticket).

Success criteria: 
- 50% reduction in high-frequency duplicate pages from burn-rate alerts during low-impact events in the staging & canary window.
- No increase in mean time to detect (MTTD) for capacity regressions above 10% vs baseline.
- Runbook provides clear troubleshooting steps for incidents tied to these alerts.

Constraints/Trade-offs: 
- Increasing suppression or hysteresis risks delayed detection of true regressions. We will mitigate via multi-signal gating and a staged canary.
- Per-customer decomposition requires more cardinality and could increase cardinality costs in our metrics pipeline. We'll prototype with a sampled subset of high-traffic customers.

Proposed solution (summary):
1) Introduce a tiered onramp with three phases: metric -> noiseless incident (dashboard and ticket) -> reduced-scope page (owner teams) -> full page if escalation persists.
2) Implement burn decomposition: compute "weighted-burn" and "local-impact" dimensions so burn-rate alerts can be scoped to customers or routes that actually cause higher SLO loss.
3) Add an "autoscaler-flap" circuit that triggers an automatic short cooldown (10m) of pagering for burn alerts if the autoscaler is actively reconciling.
4) Soft pager hysteresis: require N consecutive burn windows (configurable: default 2 of 3) before paging; keep single-window alert for a non-paging dashboard event.
5) Add cardinality-safe plan: limit per-customer decomposition to top 200 tenants by RPS for initial rollout; aggregate remainder into "other-tenants" buckets.
6) Observability & runbook changes: SLO dashboard views, per-tenant burn time-series, annotated incident history, and on-call playbook additions.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0–1: Implement metrics pipeline changes in staging (sampled per-tenant decomposition) + unit tests and simulation harness using Jan–Feb incidents.
- Week 2: Deploy to canary (10% of production traffic) with read-only dashboards and no paging. Verify false-page reduction and MTTD on simulated regressions.
- Week 3–4: Enable reduced-scope paging for canary, monitor for missed detections and cost impact.
- Week 5: Full rollout behind feature flag with quick rollback.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Missed regressions: multi-signal gating (latency, error-rate, capacity headroom) ensures at least one no-suppressing trigger remains for high-severity events.
- Metric cardinality cost: sample and limit tenants; apply rollup on ingestion.
- Complexity for on-call: update runbooks, add training session and dedicated quick-reference card.

Links & artifacts:
- Simulation notebook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/burn-sim-notebook
- Draft runbook (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/runbooks/pager-onramp-draft
- Simulation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4591
- Draft dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Sl0x/burn-decomp-playbook

Notes: This ticket is an implementable subset of the longer-term alert-classifier initiative (ENG-25432).
